title: Assistant Accountant
description:
NXTGEN is working with an established, business to recruit an Assistant Accountant for its finance team. This Assistant Accountant position offers the opportunity to develop your month-end experience within a team where people have progressed.

As Assistant Accountant, you'll work closely with the Management Accountants to prepare monthly management accounts and manufacturer reporting. You'll also work with department managers to investigate discrepancies, answer queries and help them understand the financial performance of their site.

The role combines hands-on accounting with analysis and process improvement, giving you exposure to how finance supports the day-to-day running of a motor retail business.

Key responsibilities as Assistant Accountant
- Support the preparation of monthly management accounts, including accruals and prepayments
- Prepare balance sheet reconciliations, investigate differences and follow up outstanding items
- Assist with monthly manufacturer reporting and process weekly manufacturer bonuses
- Authorise daily payments in line with company procedures
- Monitor outstanding and ageing debt, following up and reporting on overdue balances
- Support vehicle and parts stocktakes, investigate variances and report findings to management
- Respond to management accounts queries and highlight discrepancies or control concerns
- Work with the Management Accountants to identify improvements to financial processes and reporting
- Maintain accurate financial records and supporting documentation

What we're looking for

You'll have experience within a busy accounts department and be keen to build on your accounting knowledge. AAT Level 3 or an equivalent qualification is preferred, although candidates qualified by experience will also be considered.

Strong numerical skills, attention to detail and confidence using Microsoft packages are essential. You'll be comfortable investigating discrepancies, communicating with colleagues across the business and following queries through to resolution.

Knowledge of Pinnacle DMS would be useful, but isnt essential.

This Assistant Accountant role is based on site in Norwich and would suit someone looking to broaden their experience in management accounts while contributing to an expanding business.

To find out more about this Assistant Accountant opportunity, contact Grace at NXTGEN Recruitment.

title: Payroll Assistant
description:
Payroll Assistant

Location: Diss

Salary: £27,300 per annum

Hours: Full-time, 37.5 hours per week

Contract: Permanent

Working Pattern: Office-based

About the Role

My client is looking to recruit an experienced Payroll Assistant to join their established and supportive finance team in Diss.

This is a fantastic opportunity for someone with a solid background in payroll and pensions who enjoys working in a busy environment and takes pride in delivering an accurate, reliable and professional service.

You will be responsible for supporting the day-to-day payroll function, working with both clients and employees to resolve queries and ensuring payroll information is processed accurately and within strict deadlines.

Key Responsibilities

Your responsibilities will include:
- Processing payroll and pension information accurately and efficiently.
- Administering workplace pension schemes, including calculating and processing contributions.
- Liaising with pension providers and other relevant third parties when required.
- Responding to payroll queries from clients and employees, providing clear and helpful support.
- Handling payroll-related correspondence with HMRC and other external authorities.
- Dealing with matters including tax codes, PAYE, National Insurance and statutory payments.
- Maintaining accurate and up-to-date payroll records.
- Ensuring payroll information is handled confidentially and in line with GDPR requirements.
- Working to tight payroll deadlines and ensuring all work is completed accurately.
- Supporting the wider finance team with payroll-related administration where required.

About You

We are looking for someone who has:
- At least two years' experience working in payroll and pensions.
- Previous experience within an accountancy practice, payroll bureau or similar environment would be advantageous.
- Good knowledge of PAYE, National Insurance, pensions and current payroll legislation.
- Experience using payroll software; knowledge of systems such as BrightPay, Sage, Xero or QuickBooks would be beneficial.
- Excellent attention to detail and a high level of accuracy.
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to prioritise a busy workload.
- The confidence to communicate professionally with clients, employees and external organisations.
- The ability to work independently and meet strict deadlines.
- A proactive, reliable and professional approach.

What's on Offer?
- £27,300 salary
- 37.5-hour working week
- Permanent position
- Company pension
- Free on-site parking
- Health & wellbeing programme
- Company events

title: Credit Controller
company: Hays Specialist Recruitment Limited - Agency - Permanent
description:
Your new company
Are you an experienced Credit Controller who enjoys building strong customer relationships while delivering excellent cash collection results? This is an exciting opportunity to join a growing and successful organisation where your communication skills, commercial awareness, and ability to resolve outstanding debt will directly contribute to business performance and customer satisfaction.

Our client is a well-established and growing business with a strong reputation for customer service and operational excellence. They are committed to investing in their people, supporting career development, and creating a positive and collaborative working environment. As part of a successful credit control finance team, you will play a key role in managing customer accounts, maintaining strong client relationships, and ensuring the timely collection of outstanding debt.

Your new roleReporting to the Credit Manager, you will take ownership of a ledger of customer accounts, proactively managing collection activities while delivering a professional and customer-focused service. Key responsibilities will include:
- Managing and maintaining a portfolio of customer accounts.
- Chasing outstanding debt through telephone, email, and written correspondence.
- Building strong relationships with customers to encourage prompt payment.
- Negotiating payment plans and resolving account queries.
- Monitoring aged debt and reducing overdue balances.
- Investigating and resolving invoice and payment disputes.
- Allocating cash and reconciling customer accounts.
- Producing aged debt and collection reports.
- Supporting credit risk management activities.
- Working closely with internal departments to ensure excellent customer outcomes

What you'll need to succeed
You will bring previous Credit Control or Accounts Receivable experience, alongside a proven track record of confident credit collections and debt recovery. You will also possess strong customer relationship management skills, excellent communication and negotiation abilities, with the confidence to hold professional conversations regarding outstanding balances.

In addition, you will demonstrate excellent organisational and problem-solving capabilities, strong attention to detail and accuracy, experience using finance systems and Microsoft Excel, and a proactive, resilient approach with the ability to work independently and manage competing priorities effectively.

What you'll get in return
The organisation offers flexible hybrid working of 3 days in the office (NR13) with 2 days working from home, 25 days holiday plus the bank holidays, a basic salary plus a yearly bonus. Contact Andy Jarman on for more details.

What you need to do now
If you're interested in this role, click 'apply now' to forward an up-to-date copy of your CV, or call us now.
If this job isn't quite right for you, but you are looking for a new position, please contact us for a confidential discussion about your career.

This is a great opportunity to join a well-established, family-run business that is continuing to grow. The role is hands-on, tasked with supporting the day-to-day financial operations of the business and working alongside the existing accounts function.

As a key team member, you'll be responsible for keeping the financial side of the business running smoothly - using your proven accounts experience to provide integral support within the finance and administration operations, showcasing your practical and proactive approach to work.

This opportunity is based a few miles outside of Great Yarmouth and due to the remote location, a driving license and vehicle is essential.

Salary is offered at £30,000 with the role being considered both full-time or part-time at a minimum of 30 hours per week.

Benefits
- Flexible working considered
- Opportunity to work from home once established in the role
- 3 days' annual leave used for the Christmas/New Year shutdown
- Holiday entitlement increases after 2 years, from 20 up to 25 days
- Stakeholder pension scheme
- Free parking
- Bi-annual company socials
- Corporate workwear if required
- A friendly, family-run working environment with a genuinely non-hierarchical culture

The Company

Working across sectors including healthcare, education and national infrastructure, this business provides a specialist service to clients across the UK and parts of Europe.

The company has a close-knit, down-to-earth culture, with strong team morale and a genuine willingness to all muck in and get things done. As the business continues to scale, this is an excellent opportunity to become apart of the growth and join a business where everyone really does play their part.

The Day to Day
- Recording and maintaining accurate financial transactions and records
- Processing supplier invoices and making payments
- Raising customer invoices and uploading invoices to relevant portals
- Reconciling supplier statements and bank accounts
- Monitoring aged debtors and highlighting outstanding payments
- Maintaining and reviewing sales and purchase ledgers
- Supporting payroll preparation, including expenses and relevant payroll data
- Assisting with VAT returns and other financial reporting
- Supporting the preparation of monthly, quarterly and annual financial information
- Providing financial information for management review
- Identifying and highlighting discrepancies and helping to resolve them
- Supporting internal and external audits and maintaining compliance with financial procedures

You Will Have / Be
- Previous experience in a similar accounts-based role with understanding of accounting principles
- Experience using accounting software such as Sage or Xero
- Good understanding of sales and purchase ledgers
- Experience with reconciliations and balancing accounts
- Awareness of aged debtors and the importance of timely payment
- A baseline understanding of P&L
- Good attention to detail and accuracy
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to prioritise your workload
- Happy to speak to customers and suppliers regarding accounts queries when required
- A proactive, self-motivated and flexible approach

An accountancy qualification would be useful but isn't essential. What matters most is that you understand the fundamentals of accounts and have the practical experience to get on with the job.

How to Apply

Advise patients of relevant charges for private (non NHS) services, accept payment and issue receipts for same. Enter patient information on to the computer as required. Monitor and complete clinical system tasks as required by the Reception Supervisor, Practice Manager and GPs. Premises: Open up premises at the start of the day when first to arrive, de-activate alarm and make all necessary preparations to receive patients. When last to leave at the end of the day, ensure that the building is totally secured, internal lights are off and the alarm activated. Undertake any other additional duties appropriate to the post as requested by the Reception Supervisor or the Practice Manager. Attend team and practice meetings. Give results and/or information to the patient as directed by the doctors. Accept and ensure all specimens are clearly labelled and pass on to Healthcare staff for appropriate recording prior to collection by hospital transport. Confidentiality: In the course of seeking treatment, patients entrust us with, or allow us to gather, sensitive information in relation to their health and other matters. They do so in confidence and have the right to expect that staff will respect their privacy and act appropriately. In the performance of the duties outlined in this Job Description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, practice staff and other healthcare workers. They may also have access to information relating to the practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential. Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data. Health & Safety: The post-holder will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the practice Health & Safety Policy, to include: Using personal security systems within the workplace according to practice guidelines. Identifying the risks involved in work activities and undertaking such activities in a way that manages those risks. Making effective use of training to update knowledge and skills. Using appropriate infection control procedures, maintaining work areas in a tidy and safe way and free from hazards. Reporting potential risks identified to the Health and Safety Team immediately. Equality and Diversity: The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues, to include: Acting in a way that recognises the importance of peoples rights, interpreting them in a way that is consistent with practice procedures and policies, and current legislation. Respecting the privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs of patients, carers and colleagues. Behaving in a manner which is welcoming to and of the individual, is non-judgmental and respects their circumstances, feelings priorities and rights. Personal/Professional Development: The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the practice as part of this employment, such training to include: Participation in an annual individual performance review, including taking responsibility for maintaining a record of own personal and/or professional development Taking responsibility for own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work. Attending all training courses and sessions deemed as mandatory by the Practice Manager. Quality: The post-holder will strive to maintain quality within the practice, and will: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk. Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision. Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance. Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs. Effectively manage own time, workload and resources. Communication: The post-holder should recognise the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members. Communicate effectively with patients and carers. Recognise peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly. Contribution to the Implementation of Services: The post-holder will: Apply practice policies, standards and guidance. Discuss with other members of the team how the policies, standards and guidelines will affect own work. Participate in audit where appropriate.
